cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Intersection law specifies who must yield rather than?
cards.back: Intersection law specifies who must yield rather than granting an unconditional right to proceed.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Even if another driver should yield, stop or yield?
cards.back: Even if another driver should yield, stop or yield as needed to prevent a crash.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: At an unsignalized intersection, yield to crossing pedestrians whether?
cards.back: At an unsignalized intersection, yield to crossing pedestrians whether or not a crosswalk is marked.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk,?
cards.back: Yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk, even away from an intersection.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Yield when a pedestrian on a sidewalk?
cards.back: Yield when a pedestrian on a sidewalk crosses a driveway or alley.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A turning driver must yield to pedestrians?
cards.back: A turning driver must yield to pedestrians crossing with the light.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Always yield to a blind pedestrian using a?
cards.back: Always yield to a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Without contrary directions from traffic controls or police, a left-turning?
cards.back: Without contrary directions from traffic controls or police, a left-turning driver yields to oncoming traffic continuing straight.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A roundabout entrant yields to?
cards.back: A roundabout entrant yields to vehicles already circulating.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Without other traffic-control directions, drivers arriving from different roads at about?
cards.back: Without other traffic-control directions, drivers arriving from different roads at about the same time yield to vehicles on their right.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: From an alley, driveway or private road, wait for?
cards.back: From an alley, driveway or private road, wait for a clear public highway before entering.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: At a four-way stop, every vehicle stops and?
cards.back: At a four-way stop, every vehicle stops and the earliest arrival should proceed first.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: At a four-way stop, simultaneous arrivals yield to?
cards.back: At a four-way stop, simultaneous arrivals yield to the vehicle on the right.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Opposing vehicles at a four-way stop may proceed?
cards.back: Opposing vehicles at a four-way stop may proceed cautiously together while watching for turns.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Read lane-assignment signs and markings early enough to choose?
cards.back: Read lane-assignment signs and markings early enough to choose the proper intersection lane in advance.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A driver mistakenly in a turn-only lane must make?
cards.back: A driver mistakenly in a turn-only lane must make the marked turn rather than continue straight.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A driver wanting a turn but occupying a?
cards.back: A driver wanting a turn but occupying a through-only lane must continue straight.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: When adjacent lanes both permit left turns, remain in the selected lane during?
cards.back: When adjacent lanes both permit left turns, remain in the selected lane during the turn because the neighboring driver may turn simultaneously.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Cars parked on both sides facing one direction can be?
cards.back: Cars parked on both sides facing one direction can be a clue that a street is one-way.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A divided highway consists of opposing one-way roadways,?
cards.back: A divided highway consists of opposing one-way roadways, usually separated by a physical barrier.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: For a right turn onto a divided highway, select a?
cards.back: For a right turn onto a divided highway, select a safe gap in traffic approaching from the left.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: For a left turn onto a divided highway, cross the first roadway through a safe gap from the?
cards.back: For a left turn onto a divided highway, cross the first roadway through a safe gap from the left, then turn beyond the divider through a safe gap from the right.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Turning left before reaching the divider can put the vehicle into opposing?
cards.back: Turning left before reaching the divider can put the vehicle into opposing traffic; heed WRONG WAY and DO NOT ENTER signs.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: At a two-way stop, crossing a thirty miles per hour road takes about a six-second?
cards.back: At a two-way stop, crossing a thirty miles per hour road takes about a six-second gap in both directions, or about a clear block each way.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Before a right turn, scan left, ahead, right and left again, allowing about?
cards.back: Before a right turn, scan left, ahead, right and left again, allowing about eight seconds to a vehicle approaching from the left.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Before a left turn, make sure oncoming traffic leaves a?
cards.back: Before a left turn, make sure oncoming traffic leaves a clear gap and cross-street traffic is stopped.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Turning left from a minor road onto a major road calls for?
cards.back: Turning left from a minor road onto a major road calls for a nine-second gap to traffic approaching from the right.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Opposing left-turning drivers avoid tangling by turning before the center crossing?
cards.back: Opposing left-turning drivers avoid tangling by turning before the center crossing point and entering the lane nearest the centerline.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Do not begin a left turn until every lane to be crossed is?
cards.back: Do not begin a left turn until every lane to be crossed is visibly clear and the turn can be completed safely.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A jughandle makes a left turn by following a right-side curved lane?
cards.back: A jughandle makes a left turn by following a right-side curved lane back to a signalized crossing of the main road.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Traffic circulates counterclockwise through roundabouts and traffic circles,?
cards.back: Traffic circulates counterclockwise through roundabouts and traffic circles, entering and leaving with right turns.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Roundabout entries have yield signs?
cards.back: Roundabout entries have yield signs and pavement yield lines.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Most roundabouts have approach destination signs?
cards.back: Most roundabouts have approach destination signs identifying the exit roads.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Approach a roundabout slowly and prepare to yield?
cards.back: Approach a roundabout slowly and prepare to yield to people in the crosswalk.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: At the yield line, look left, yield to circulating traffic?
cards.back: At the yield line, look left, yield to circulating traffic and enter only through an adequate gap.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Inside a roundabout, continue counterclockwise?
cards.back: Inside a roundabout, continue counterclockwise toward the intended exit.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Use the right turn signal as?
cards.back: Use the right turn signal as the roundabout exit approaches.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Yield to pedestrians when entering?
cards.back: Yield to pedestrians when entering and leaving a roundabout.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: If an emergency vehicle approaches before entry, do not?
cards.back: If an emergency vehicle approaches before entry, do not enter the roundabout and pull aside.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: If already circulating when an emergency vehicle approaches, leave the?
cards.back: If already circulating when an emergency vehicle approaches, leave the roundabout and pull aside rather than stopping inside.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A bicyclist may use a roundabout as a vehicle or pedestrian;?
cards.back: A bicyclist may use a roundabout as a vehicle or pedestrian; the vehicle role follows the same traffic rules.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Do not overtake a bicyclist operating as?
cards.back: Do not overtake a bicyclist operating as a vehicle inside a roundabout.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Pedestrians use crosswalks and splitter islands to?
cards.back: Pedestrians use crosswalks and splitter islands to cross the roundabout's legs.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Entering a curve too fast can carry a vehicle?
cards.back: Entering a curve too fast can carry a vehicle straight ahead instead of along the bend.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: The greatest speed reductions are needed on sharp?
cards.back: The greatest speed reductions are needed on sharp curves with wet or icy surfaces.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Reduce speed before entering a?
cards.back: Reduce speed before entering a curve to maintain control.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Curve warnings are usually yellow diamonds, while a ninety-degree bend may?
cards.back: Curve warnings are usually yellow diamonds, while a ninety-degree bend may have a large arrow on a yellow rectangle.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Chevron signs along sharp curves help show the direction of the?
cards.back: Chevron signs along sharp curves help show the direction of the bend, especially at night or in poor visibility.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: On a right curve, stay slightly right of lane?
cards.back: On a right curve, stay slightly right of lane center; on a left curve, stay centered.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Reduce speed more as?
cards.back: Reduce speed more as curve sharpness increases.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Watch opposing traffic in a curve because a?
cards.back: Watch opposing traffic in a curve because a speeding driver may enter your lane.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Look ahead along the curve's inside edge for steering guidance, checking each?
cards.back: Look ahead along the curve's inside edge for steering guidance, checking each bend in a sequence as far ahead as visible.
